subject: Payment path options: EUR settlement vs USD collection and midpoint bank charges
messages:
From: Oliver Greene <oliver.greene@papertrail.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Natalie Cho <nat.cho@papertrail.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 08:32:00 +0000
Subject: Collecting payment — can we pay EUR locally or do you need USD?

Hi Priya,

Quick one from our side as we prepare the June invoice (attached draft): do you require collection in USD into your US nostro, or can we pay in EUR to your EU account? Our AP team prefers to pay in EUR to avoid FX on our side, but their bank has warned there may be a correspondent bank / intermediary charge if the payment routes through USD rails.

Specifically: who should bear intermediary/correspondent fees (OUR/SHA/BEN), and do you have guidance on the cleanest path to avoid surprises on our reconciliation? Also, are there any VAT/reverse-charge implications if we pay EUR to an Irish entity vs USD to a US entity?

I attached the draft invoice and our bank's suggested wire template. Happy to hop on a quick call if easier.

Thanks,
Oliver
CFO, PaperTrail Inc.

Attachment stubs: 2027-06-14-Invoice-3784.pdf (PDF), wire_template_PaperTrail.xlsx (Excel)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Greene <oliver.greene@papertrail.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 13:07:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Collecting payment — can we pay EUR locally or do you need USD?

Hi Oliver — thanks for the clear note and the draft invoice. Looping in Laura (billing ops) and Marissa (recon) so we have the right operational view.

Short answer: we can accept EUR into our Irish collection account, which avoids an on-us USD conversion on your side. A few practical notes to avoid intermediary charges and VAT surprises:

- Beneficiary instructions: use SHA by default (shared fees) only if you accept small intermediary costs and want to preserve your bank's routing preferences. If you need guaranteed net delivery to Redwood, request OUR (Payer covers all intermediary fees) and confirm with your bank the correspondent chain — they may add a mid-bank charge.
- Recommended path: EUR --> Redwood (Ireland) IBAN (SEPA) if both banks are in SEPA zone. This is the cheapest. If PaperTrail's bank attempts a cross-border EUR payment via a USD correspondent (rare), intermediary fees can be applied.
- If you must pay USD: instruct OUR and we will gross-up the invoice (we can provide a gross-up calculation) or accept SHA and document the expected deduction so reconciliation matches.
- VAT: if the invoice is issued by Redwood Ireland (we've attached the invoice draft showing VAT reverse-charge line) you should not be charged Irish VAT under B2B reverse charge if you have a valid VAT number. We'll need your VAT ID on the remit details. If paying USD to Redwood US entity, VAT isn't relevant but local withholding rules may apply depending on entity structure.

Operational asks for a clean EUR flow (fastest/cheapest):
1) Confirm payer VAT ID (if applying reverse-charge).
2) Use the IBAN and SWIFT for Redwood Ireland from the attached wire template (we've flagged the preferred SEPA rails).
3) Set the payment instruction to SHA unless you explicitly confirm OUR. If YOU choose SHA, please request your bank to include an "OMT/OUR if possible" note in internal remittance — some banks will route via an intermediary and tag fees differently.

Laura / Marissa: can you confirm the exact IBAN and whether we can accept a net EUR amount (i.e., Redwood absorbs any bank deduction) for this customer if they push SHA? I can offer a one-off concession if necessary but want ops to confirm how recon will handle short amounts.

Best,
Priya
Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: invoice draft attached referenced above.

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com

Subject: RE: Collecting payment — can we pay EUR locally or do you need USD?

Thanks Priya / Oliver — quick operational notes from billing:

- Confirmed account: Redwood Ireland Ltd (EUR) — IBAN IE12REDB00012345678901, BIC REDWIE2D. Use SEPA rails when both sides support SEPA.
- Intermediary fees: if payer selects SHA, any correspondent/intermediary fees are typically deducted by the payer's bank (amount received will be invoice minus those deductions). We generally ask for OUR for full-value receipt. For one-off convenience we can accept SHA as long as PaperTrail acknowledges potential small shortfalls and we will issue a short-payment memo.
- Reconciliation: Marissa will accept a remittance advice file. If the amount received is short more than EUR 50 we escalate to a manual reconciliation and request proof of outbound fees from PaperTrail's bank.

Oliver — can you confirm whether your AP system can send the remittance advice (CSV or PDF) to accounting@redwood.com and include the payment reference: PTL-4379? Also please send your VAT number if applying reverse-charge.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Head of Billing Operations
Redwood Inference

Thanks Laura — yes we can send remittance advice. Our bank indicated they may route via an intermediate correspondent for certain EUR-to-IE transfers because our branch consolidates cross-border traffic, which could generate a single intermediary fee of ~EUR 15-25. PaperTrail prefers not to chase small deductions. We'd therefore like Redwood to accept SHA and we will set the payment amount so the invoice net is received (i.e., we will add an estimated corridor fee to the payment to cover common cases). Can you confirm Redwood is okay with that approach?

Also attached is our VAT number and the remittance template.

Oliver

Hi Oliver / Team — confirmed on our side:

- Accepting the SHA + payer-add-on approach is fine for this invoice (one-off). Please add an extra EUR 20 as a corridor buffer to the payment to cover likely intermediary charges; we'll reconcile and issue a short-payment memo only if the received delta exceeds EUR 50.
- Please set payment reference: PTL-4379 and include remittance to accounting@redwood.com.
- We will mark the invoice as reverse-charge pending receipt of your VAT ID (we have the PDF you attached). Once payment clears we will send a payment confirmation and an updated accounting statement.
- For future invoices, if you plan to always pay EUR from the UK, we can issue an EU-local invoice (Redwood Ireland) and provide a standing instruction to avoid intermediary fees — happy to set that up with your AP team.

Thanks — Marissa
